svg.title: tile march
svg.text: mm_tiled_1to1<32>: A and B tiles march along K through shared memory
block = 32 × 32 threads = one 32 × 32 tile of C; loop t = 0 … 1023 (32768 / 32)
A: the block's 32 rows × 32768 columns (1024 tiles)
B: 32768 rows × the
block's 32 columns
C tile [32, 32]
shared memory (on the SM): 2 × 4 KB
__syncthreads()
1. load: each thread copies 1 A + 1 B element
A tile t → sA, B tile t → sB

g.text: 1. load: each thread copies 1 A + 1 B element
A tile t → sA, B tile t → sB

svg.text: 2. __syncthreads()
wait until both tiles are complete

g.text: wait until both tiles are complete

svg.text: 3. compute: 32 FMAs per thread
sA row ty × sB column tx, from shared

g.text: sA row ty × sB column tx, from shared

svg.text: 4. __syncthreads()
nobody overwrites a tile others still read

g.text: nobody overwrites a tile others still read

svg.text: Each global element is loaded once per
block and then read 32 times from
shared memory: global traffic ÷ 32.
The C tile darkens as partial sums
from each pair of tiles pile up in
the threads' acc registers.
animated: four of the 1024 steps; each pair of tiles is staged, synced, consumed, synced again
